qt: to the Commission Leire Pajín (S&D), Sandra Gómez López (S&D) Subject:

The safeguarding of democracy and the rule of law, human dignity and justice, as well as the rights and remembrance of the victims of dictatorships and totalitarian regimes, form part of the Union’s founding principles. However, certain institutions, with a view to historical revisionism and glorification, are reinstating fascist symbols in public spaces, thereby breaching regulations on historical remembrance and undermining the very foundations of the Union. The case of Albaida, where a Francoist cross is being re-erected in a public space where 18 victims of the Franco regime were shot1, is an example of the presence and reinstatement of anti-democratic symbols in Europe. What is more, the glorification of European dictatorships and their repressive practices makes it harder to pass on our history to new generations, thereby jeopardising European and democratic values. Against this background: 1.

What view does the Commission take of the restoration of monuments to dictatorships such as that of Franco in respect of the fundamental values and principles enshrined in the Charter of Fundamental Rights?
What measures is it taking to combat revisionism and promote a rigorously lucid European remembrance that recognises the victims of these regimes?

Does the Commission intend to step up support, through the Citizens, Equality, Rights and Values programme, for projects promoting remembrance, critical reflection on history and raising awareness of crimes committed by European dictatorships?
